Body:
Ok, good finding @gaetan-puleo , while not perfect adding <|think|> to all messages make 26B also think, it may keep track of a previous <|think|> but it may not, so if the prompt needs thinking it's better to be explicit

Conversation: https://opncd.ai/share/Pbdp7w2L

Note how it thinks again to reply to the message: "hmmm, is that true?"

but the third message fails to think

Then I explicitly include the <|think|> again in the last message "<|think|> give me a better argument" and it thinks again.

It's interesting, likely useful, adding <|think|> to "systemPrompt" to opencode.json did **nothing** .... but adding to "prompt" works for all prompts, now the model is always thinking, which was the thing I wanted to achieve, models that don't reason are faster, but overall produce less quality agentic coding

Conversation with prompt added: https://opncd.ai/share/a7uTEcIT

Note in this case, it's  thinking for al prompts, I purposely prompted questions that would trigger large thinking blocks, to add some pressure on the KV cache, to check if the model "forgets" that it has to think

I'd like to ask the maintainers to reconsider this feature request. While #21789 was auto-closed by the bot for not following the template format, the underlying feature request is valuable.

**My use case:** I'm working on complex coding tasks where I need Opus-level intelligence for strategic planning, but Opus is too expensive to run for entire conversations. Anthropic's Advisor Tool (released April 9, 2026) solves this perfectly - it lets Sonnet consult Opus mid-generation for guidance, giving near-Opus quality at mostly-Sonnet cost.

I built a workaround script that uses the advisor tool externally, but it runs outside OpenCode's context so the advisor can't see my codebase. Native support would allow Opus to provide strategic guidance while still having full access to project files and OpenCode's tools.

Could the team please share why this was marked "not planned"? Is there a technical limitation, or is this feature not aligned with OpenCode's roadmap?

Reference: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/advisor-tool

I'm experiencing the same issue on my MacBook Pro 16-inch (2019) running macOS Sonoma 14.7.8 (23H730). Environment details: - Terminal: Apple Terminal (macOS built-in) - $TERM: `xterm-256color` - $TERM_PROGRAM: `Apple_Terminal` - $COLORTERM: not set (empty) The built-in macOS Terminal does not support Truecolor (24-bit color) and does not set `$COLORTERM`, which appears to be the root cause of the broken theme rendering. Setting `export COLORTERM=truecolor` does not resolve the issue in Apple Terminal. However, switching to iTerm2 fixes the problem completely, themes render correctly there. This suggests the issue is specific to Apple Terminal's color handling and cannot be worked around from within the shell alone. Happy to provide further details or test any fixes. Yeah, the workaround you mentioned (disabling both `ruff` and `uv`) is what I ended up doing for now.

My main point though is that having these as two separate formatter toggles does not really make sense. According to the official docs, `uv format` is equivalent to running `ruff format` in the project root:
https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/#uv-format

So from a user perspective, this is not a different formatter—it’s just another way to invoke Ruff.

Because of that, the current behavior is pretty confusing:

* I disable `formatter.ruff`, but Python files are still formatted
* OpenCode silently uses `uv format` instead

I think this should either be unified into a single Python formatter setting, or documented more clearly.
